Why 1b. The new rules for fairway side slope and green contour (docs/COURSE-DESIGN.md, 10 November) landed while round 1 was being built. This print brings the same layout up to them; routing, yardages, tees, bunkers and hazards are as before.

Fairways lean, with a purpose. Every par 4 and 5 landing area now falls 2–3.5% across the line, measured round each target. Holes with water on the right lean away from it: the 4th (3% at the bend, toward the left), the 7th (3.5%, over the crest) and the 8th (3.5%, away from the swamp). The 2nd leans 3% toward the cycads, so the high right side has the angle. The 1st falls 3% to the right, feeding drives round the corner toward the green's open side; the 6th falls 2.5% off the knoll toward the arch side.

The strong one: the 9th's ramp. 6% across, falling away from the cliff to the right, so the second is played with the ball above your feet. The catch bunker on the right is a little bigger to take what runs off.

Greens: moderate, with one feature each on seven. A 1.5–2% fall on every green, plus: the 1st a bowl in the back-left lobe; the 2nd a tier 0.5 m up at the back; the 3rd a low spine across the peanut's waist; the 6th a shelf 0.6 m up at the back-left end (the bold green of the nine); the 7th a bowl in its back half; the 8th a bowl in the right end of the T's bar; the 9th a spine from the left horn to the back. The 4th (its false front is the feature) and the 5th (a long iron beside the pool) stay flatter.
Pin areas. Every green has two or three areas 10 m across at 3% or less; the pins sit at 0.9–2%. To make room, the 3rd, 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th greens are a little bigger (now 480–620 m²).

New on each hole page: a diagram of the green (5 cm contours, arrows downhill, red over 3%, pin areas dashed), and a Contour line with the green's typical slope, its shape beyond the fall, pin areas, and the fairway lean at each target.
